source_text: Τὸ πλησίον αὐτοῦ λαλεῖ εἰρηνικὰ, καὶ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔχει τὴν ἐχθράν κτλ. Οὐκ ἂν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ φαρισαῖοι τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων πολὺ τὸ οὐαὶ παρὰ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἐκληρονόμησαν, εἰ μὴ διὰ τὴν ὑπόκρισιν· ἐν γὰρ τοῖς ἐλέγχοις τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐπαύσατο κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν προλέγων ὁ Κύριος· Οὐαὶ ὑμὶν, 592 γραμματεῖς καὶ φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταὶ, κεκονιαμένους τάφους ἀποκαλῶν αὐτοὺς, οἱ ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ὡραῖοι, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πά-σης ἀκαθαρσίας. Ἐὰν γάρ τι εἰς τὸν πλησίον ἀγαθὸν ἐργασώμεθα διὰ τῆς ἀνυποκρίτου ἀγάπης, ἀ-κούομεν παρὰ τοῦ σωτῆρος· Ἐφ' ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε. Οὕτω δὲ καὶ εἴ τι φαῦλον διὰ τῆς ἀπατηλῆς καὶ μιαρᾶς ὑποκρίσεως, ἢ καὶ διὰ ὁποιασοῦν ἑτέρας ἁ-μαρτίας, εἰς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἐνδειξώμεθα, ὁ-μοίως ἁμαρτάνομεν καὶ εἰς τὸν Θεόν. ∆εῖνον οὖν ἡ ὑπόκρισις, ἀδελφοὶ, καὶ πολέμιον· καὶ κεκρυμμένος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ δόλος, εἰς ἀπά-την τῶν ἁπλῶς προσφερομένων, τοῖς ἀγά-πην κεκτημένοις, ἄλλα μὲν ἐκ στόματος λαλοῦσα, ἄλλα δὲ ἐν στέρνοις φέρουσα, δελεάζει. Οὐκ ἀγαθὸν ἡ ὑπερηφανία, ψευδοδοξίαν ἔχουσα πολλήν· δῆλον γὰρ, δῆλον, ὡς πᾶν ἀγαθὸν τέλειον θεόθεν ἔρχεται· καὶ οὐκ ἔστι ληπτὸν ἄλλως ἀνθρώπῳ, ὡς ὄντως ἀ-ληθέστατον εἶναι πάντων τὸ εἰρημένον, ὅτι δέοι τὸν αὐχοῦντα ἐπί τινι τούτῳ μόνον σε-μνύνεσθαι, καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ συνιέναι καὶ γινώσ-κειν ὅτι Κύριος αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν ἔλεος καὶ κρίμα καὶ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ ἐστὶ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἀρέσκεται γὰρ τὸ θεῖον τῷ τοιούτῳ ἀνθρώπῳ, μόνιμά τε καὶ βέβαια φέρει διὰ παντὸς τὰ ἀγαθὰ, ὅταν τούτῳ τὴν αἰτίαν ἀποδιδῷ τῷν παρόντων ἀγαθῶν τῷ ὄντως αἰτιωτάτῳ, ᾧ τὴν αἰτίαν ἀναφέρειν δεῖ καὶ τοῦ μένειν τὰ ἀγαθά.
thought_title: Hypocrisy and hidden deceit are deadly; every good or evil done to a brother is done to God
orientation: Gregory opens his commentary on Jeremiah by applying the prophet's warning about a neighbor who speaks peace while harboring enmity to the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees.
pass_a_gloss: His neighbor speaks peaceful things, and in himself he has the enmity, etc. The scribes and the Pharisees of the people of the Jews would not have inherited much of the woe from the Savior, if not because of the hypocrisy; for in the refutations of their sins the Lord did not cease foretelling on every occasion: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, calling them whitewashed tombs, who outwardly appear beautiful to men, but inwardly are full of bones of the dead and of all uncleanness. For if we do any good to the neighbor through unhypocritical love, we hear from the Savior: Inasmuch as you did it to one of these my least brothers, you did it to me. And so also if we show any evil toward the brother through deceptive and defiled hypocrisy, or also through any other sin whatsoever, we sin likewise also against God. Hypocrisy therefore is terrible, brothers, and hostile; and deceit hidden in the heart, for the deception of those who approach simply, of those who possess love, speaking one set of things from the mouth, but carrying another set of things in the breast, entices. Pride is not good, having much empty glory; for it is clear, clear, that every perfect good comes from God; and it is not obtainable otherwise by man, so that truly most true of all is the saying, that the one who boasts in anything must glory in this alone, and in understanding and knowing that the Lord himself is the one who does mercy and judgment and righteousness, and in this is the will of God. For the divine is pleased with such a man, and brings good things lasting and firm through all time, when he assigns the cause of the present good things to this one, to the one who is truly most causative, to whom it is necessary to refer the cause also of the good things remaining.

choices.why: Glossary term; renders the outward pretense of piety that conceals inward evil.
Literal rendering of the image of tombs coated with whitewash, matching the Savior's words.
Keeps the negation of hypocrisy explicit, as in the source, rather than substituting a positive term.
Glossary term; renders the deceptive self-esteem accompanying pride.
Captures the baiting or luring force of hidden deceit against the simple.

choices.english: to the one who is truly most causative
choices.why: Literal superlative rendering of αἰτιωτάτῳ, preserving the emphatic attribution of causality to God.

pass_b_english: "Each one speaks peace to his neighbor, but holds enmity within himself," and so on (Jeremiah 9:8). The scribes and Pharisees of the Jewish people would not have inherited so great a "woe" from the Savior if it were not for hypocrisy. For in exposing their sins, the Lord never stopped warning them on every occasion: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites," calling them whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful to people on the outside but inside are full of dead bones and every kind of uncleanness (Matthew 23:27). If we do something good to a neighbor through unhypocritical love, we hear from the Savior: "Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of mine, you did for me" (Matthew 25:40). In the same way, if we do something evil to a brother through deceptive and defiled hypocrisy, or through any other sin whatever, we sin against God just as much. Hypocrisy, brothers, is therefore a terrible and hostile thing. And deceit hidden in the heart, meant to entrap those who come forward in simplicity, speaks one thing with the mouth while carrying another in the breast, and so it deceives those who possess love. Pride is not good, since it carries with it much empty glory. For it is clear—very clear—that every perfect good comes from God. It cannot be received by a human being in any other way, so that what has been said is truly the most certain of all: the one who boasts should glory only in this, in understanding and knowing that the Lord himself is the one who shows mercy and judgment and righteousness, and in this is the will of God (Jeremiah 9:24). For the divine takes pleasure in such a person and always produces good things that are lasting and secure, when that person attributes the cause of the good things he has to the one who is truly the ultimate cause—the one to whom he must also attribute the cause of the good things remaining.

problems.why: 'Entices' suggests allurement; δελεάζει here means deceives/beguiles into harm, stronger than mere enticement.
'Most causative' is not English idiom; means 'the truest cause' or 'ultimate cause'. Obscures meaning.
problems.fix: the one who is truly the ultimate cause
problems.ruling: 'Most causative' is not natural English for αἰτιωτάτῳ; 'true/ultimate cause' needed; obscures meaning.

edits.old: and so it entices those who possess love
edits.new: and so it deceives those who possess love

edits.old: the one who is truly most causative
edits.new: the one who is truly the ultimate cause

problems.why: τὸ θεῖον is 'the divine' or 'divinity/God' but subject is neuter singular; 'is pleased' (Ἀρέσκεται) is passive/reflexive, better 'takes pleasure'.
problems.fix: the divine takes pleasure in such a person

problems.why: δεῖνον means 'terrible, dreadful, fearful' not 'deadly'; πολέμιον means 'hostile, an enemy'—'deadly' overstates and misreads.
problems.ruling: δεῖνον means 'terrible/dreadful,' not 'deadly'; mistranslates the word's meaning.

problems.quote: brings good things that are lasting and secure
problems.source_quote: μόνιμά τε καὶ βέβαια φέρει διὰ παντὸς τὰ ἀγαθά
problems.why: φέρει here means 'produces, yields, brings forth' not 'brings'; 'through all things' (διὰ παντὸς) means 'always, continually' not 'through all things'.
problems.fix: and always produces goods that are lasting and secure
problems.ruling: διὰ παντός means 'always/continually,' not 'through all things'; mistranslates the adverbial phrase.

problems.why: Subject shifts: God produces goods when the person gives cause/attribution to God; 'he' ambiguous, could read as God attributing to himself.
problems.fix: when that person attributes the cause
problems.ruling: ὅταν + τούτῳ...ἀποδιδῷ: subject is the person attributing to God; 'he' is genuinely ambiguous, risks misreading.

edits.old: the divine is pleased with such a person
edits.new: the divine takes pleasure in such a person

edits.old: Hypocrisy, brothers, is therefore a deadly and hostile thing.
edits.new: Hypocrisy, brothers, is therefore a terrible and hostile thing.

edits.old: and brings good things that are lasting and secure through all things
edits.new: and always produces good things that are lasting and secure

edits.old: when he attributes the cause of the good things he has
edits.new: when that person attributes the cause of the good things he has

fixed: The 'deadly and hostile' problem was real: δεῖνον means 'terrible, dreadful,' not 'deadly.'
The 'brings good things that are lasting and secure' problem was real: φέρει means 'produces/yields,' and διὰ παντὸς means 'always/continually.'
The 'when he attributes' problem was real: the subject is the person, not God.
The 'the divine is pleased' problem was real: ἀρέσκεται is better rendered 'takes pleasure.'

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'hypocrisy' as the rendering for ὑπόκρισις; 'unhypocritical' violates this fixed term.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνυπόκριτος is a distinct adjective meaning 'sincere/unhypocritical'; not the noun ὑπόκρισις. No glossary violation.
